clue.text: Dismisses porters engaged within tourist area

explanation.definitionFit: This national park of hills and valleys is a popular holiday destination in northern England.

clue.text: As I might say to my informant, I totally agree!

definitions.text: As I might say to my informant, I totally agree!

parts.words: As I might say to my informant, I totally agree!
parts.note: an emphatic catchphrase of agreement is, read literally, a remark addressed to someone passing on information

explanation.surface: A speaker wholeheartedly agreeing with someone who has just told them something.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom expresses strong agreement; read literally it simply states that the other person is informing the speaker, which fits an informant.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial phrase is a sarcastic way of saying a point is already obvious and agreed.

explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns HER into REH. The Ouse is a crossword-favourite English river.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehouse someone is to provide them with a new home, a fresh place to live.

clue.text: One tending to be broke?

clue.text: Increase a reduced volume — turn sound up about a quarter
